terra.problem: The text does not say the plunder was left in a hall. Marking an invented event as a guess does not establish it.
Joab sends messengers after Abner; the text does not say he goes after Abner himself.
Joab returns after Abner has left, but the text does not establish that Joab was away for the entire visit.
Saying David is not ashamed asserts a feeling the text does not give. He says he and his kingdom are guiltless.
“No debt” asserts more than David says. He does not mention a debt.
The text says David walked behind the funeral bier; it does not say whether he hung back at an edge.
The text says the people wept more after the lament, but does not explicitly say the lament moved them further.
The text says the people wept more; it does not say they did not leave.
“He kept the day for mourning” adds a purpose and a duration that the text does not state.
David takes an oath not to eat before sunset. The text does not say whether he later ate with the people.
The explanation states as an accomplished fact that David ate nothing before sunset. The text records his oath, not its fulfillment.
The text says all the people took note and that all the troops and all Israel were convinced. It does not say they all saw what David did.
The text does not say all the troops and all Israel watched David mourn all day. This guesses at an event, not a feeling.
“He leaves the repaying with the LORD” adds a decision beyond David's stated request that the LORD repay the evildoer.
